name: Allegra Spender
role: Australian Member of Parliament for Wentworth
description: Australian parliamentarian assessed through tax reform, climate policy, public integrity and civil equality.

axes.brief: Her programme emphasises competitive representation, transparent donations, parliamentary accountability and expert-informed policy.
axes.counterEvidence: Community consultation and independent advice do not establish that every issue must be decided by binding public vote.

axes.brief: She expressly defends disagreement, protest, criticism and offence alongside prohibiting intentional serious vilification and protecting whistleblowers.
axes.counterEvidence: Protecting expression does not repeal bounded safety rules; support for strong border laws is qualified by objections to rushed restrictions on asylum rights.

axes.brief: She supports diverse communities, equal recognition and Indigenous respect within a shared Australian civic life.
axes.counterEvidence: Representation of Wentworth’s Jewish community is not evidence that a single religion should dominate national culture.

axes.brief: She supports stronger humanitarian intake, permanent protection and community sponsorship while explicitly retaining secure borders and law.
axes.counterEvidence: More humane asylum policy is not unconditional residence for every irregular entrant; housing capacity and lawful pathways remain relevant.

qualifications.7: Labour needs and capacity-based administration both matter; no blanket employer-demand rule is documented.
qualifications.8: Economic and housing benefits must be balanced; the record does not establish a general reduction regardless of benefit.
qualifications.12: Education and regulated visas both matter; graduation alone is not a fully specified entitlement.

axes.brief: She values defence capability but questions AUKUS cost, strategic purpose and delivery and seeks public scrutiny.
axes.counterEvidence: Her statement that some submarines are preferable to none is direct counter-evidence to treating her as an absolute pacifist.

qualifications.1: Defensive national interests and opposition to unexamined escalation make the broad non-attack force permission conditional.
qualifications.13: Credible deterrence and diplomacy conflict under a general threat-for-concessions rule.

axes.brief: Climate cooperation and humanitarian principles accompany independent Australian decision-making and scrutiny of security alliances.
axes.counterEvidence: International cooperation does not transfer every domestic law, monetary decision or entry decision to external institutions.

qualifications.3: Domestic law and accepted international obligations provide competing responsibilities.
qualifications.7: National prosperity and common obligations both matter, making an unconditional hierarchy too broad.

axes.brief: She encourages private business, investment and competition while supporting public infrastructure and affordable housing institutions.
axes.counterEvidence: Support for public funding is not necessarily public ownership; no programme to nationalise banks or extractive industry is documented.

qualifications.8: Public financing capacity and private commercial banking offer different tools; no general public-bank programme is established.

axes.brief: Her business and productivity programme suggests open competition and trade with proportionate security and environmental safeguards.
axes.counterEvidence: Domestic transition investment is not itself an import tariff; trade-specific answers beyond the programme remain contextual estimates.

qualifications.5: Supply resilience and import affordability compete.
qualifications.7: New-industry support and lower consumer costs give opposing reasons for import restrictions.
qualifications.9: Agricultural resilience and competition provide competing considerations.
qualifications.11: Retaliation may defend access but can increase costs.

axes.brief: She proposes a competitive business environment and productive capital allocation with selective climate investment and accountable public expenditure.
axes.counterEvidence: Tax incentives and guardrails are distinct from compulsory national production or government control of all bank lending.

axes.brief: Her tax proposal shifts burden from work toward investment income while retaining fiscal neutrality and lowering income tax rates.
axes.counterEvidence: Reducing concessions on asset earnings is not a tax on wealth balances; she explicitly opposes taxation of unrealised gains and does not propose higher total taxation.

qualifications.2: Income fairness and reward for effort are both purposes, rather than either unlimited equalisation or rejection of redistribution.
qualifications.8: Targeted welfare and humane assistance do not establish arbitrary expiry for all capable recipients.
qualifications.10: Budget restraint and adequate social provision pull in opposing directions.

axes.brief: Civil equal-rights policy and protection against discrimination apply independently of religious approval.
axes.counterEvidence: Opposing discrimination in religious schools does not prohibit personal faith or erase all religious holidays and community traditions.

qualifications.9: Civic inclusion and freedom of religious expression give competing considerations for every official ceremony.
qualifications.14: Religious and charitable institutional purposes may overlap; no specific tax-exemption programme is documented.

axes.brief: She supports LGBTQ equality, gender-affirming care and freedom from religious-school exclusion alongside wider civic inclusion.
axes.counterEvidence: Equal recognition does not require every inherited custom to be immediately discarded.

qualifications.14: Change and institutional stability both have value.
qualifications.16: Traditions may be freely retained without a universal preservation obligation.

axes.brief: Her programme combines business innovation and clean-energy development with environmental protection and evidence-informed safeguards.
axes.counterEvidence: Infrastructure support qualifies blanket habitat preservation; human enhancement is less directly documented and remains a cautious analogy.

qualifications.11: Autonomy and uncertain irreversible neurological effects give opposing considerations.

axes.brief: Constituency consultation and protected communities coexist with national climate, tax and social programmes.
axes.counterEvidence: Local participation is not unlimited secession authority; federal coordination does not establish one centrally directed police system.

qualifications.2: Constitutional allocation and national programme delivery divide responsibility.
qualifications.14: Fair national taxation and regional fiscal discretion give competing considerations.

axes.brief: Her education and opportunity work and explanations of systemic disadvantage emphasise social circumstances while allowing individual biological variation.
axes.counterEvidence: Fiscal and equality arguments do not quantify every psychological trait; the specific culture–nature answers are educated contextual assumptions.

sources.title: Allegra Spender — biography and political positions

religion.reason: The public biography reviewed does not establish a declared religious identity. Constituency religion and school history are not substituted for her own identity.
